"''If you can't find it here, it's not worth finding.|Willi and Luthen Rael discuss Ferrix|audio=NeverChanges-Willi-ThatWouldBeMe.flac|}} '''Ferrix''' was a sparsely populated [[Color|reddish]], barren, rocky [[planet]] with very little [[plant]] life located in the [[Morlani system]] of the [[Free Trade sector]], a formerly corporate-run subsector of the [[Xappyh sector]] at an intersecting portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories]] and the [[New Territories]]. Located at the coordinates Q-3 of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]], the planet was situated at a junction between multiple important [[Hyperspace route|Hyperspace lanes]] including the [[Hydian Way]]. Ferrix's people, the [[Ferrixian]]s, lived in tight-knit communities built around the industry of scrapping and salvaging [[Starship]]s, with the largest of these communities known as [[Ferrix City]], which was built over a wasteland on the planet. Over time, Ferrix's salvage markets became reputed to hold some of the best second-hand parts inventory in [[The galaxy]], with an old saying stating that if something could not be found on Ferrix, it was not worth finding. By the [[Republic Era|time]] of the [[Galactic Republic]], Ferrix was a member world of the Republic. As such, during the [[High Republic Era]]'s [[Nihil conflict]], the [[Nihil]] [[Pirate|marauders]] from [[Lourna Dee's Tempest]] carried out a [[raid on Ferrix]] between [[231 BBY]] and [[230 BBY]]. Later in the era during [[228 BBY]], Ferrix was also the site of a [[Hostage negotiation on Ferrix|hostage negotiation]] that was overseen by [[Jedi Master]] [[Kantam Sy]]. During the [[Imperial Era]], Ferrix was controlled by the [[Galactic Empire]] and overseen by the [[Consolidated Holdings of Preox-Morlana Corporation]]. However, this status was revoked following investigations of rebel activity. This eventually led to the [[Ferrix Riot|Rix Road riot]] that saw the citizens of Ferrix fight back against the occupying Imperial personnel. ==Description== [[File:FerrixLocation.png|thumb|left|200px|Ferrix sat at the junction between several key Hyperspace lanes including the Hydian Way]] Ferrix was a rocky and barren [[color|amber-colored]] terrestrial [[planet]] located in the [[Morlani system]] of the [[Free Trade sector]], a subsector of the [[Xappyh sector]] in an intersecting portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories]] and the [[New Territories]]. The planet was located at the coordinates Q-3 in the [[Standard Galactic Grid]], and was located at the junction between several key [[Hyperspace route|Hyperspace lanes]]{{Databank|ferrix|Ferrix}} including the [[Hydian Way]]. Ferrix was 7,914 [[kilometer]]s in diameter, and had an [[Local year|orbital period]] of 462 [[Standard day]]s. The surface of the world was dominated by large rocky [[mountain]]s and [[mesa]]s, vast desolate wastelands, and pockets of blue oceans. During the winter months, the [[temperature]] was cold, with the ground often becoming covered in layers of snow. ==History== ===Republic Era=== The [[smuggler]] [[Radicaz Dobbs]] knew of the chimes of Ferrix''[[The High Republic: Path of Vengeance]]'' by [[382 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: The High Republic Character Encyclopedia]]'' dates the events of ''[[The High Republic: Path of Vengeance]]'' to [[382 BBY]]. during the [[High Republic Era]]. Between [[231 BBY]] and [[230 BBY]]''[[The High Republic: Tempest Breaker]]'' establishes that the raid on Ferrix took place between the [[Defense of the Restitution|defense of the ''Restitution'']] and the [[destruction of Starlight Beacon]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[231 BBY]] and [[230 BBY]], respectively. during the [[Nihil conflict]], [[Nihil]] [[Pirate|marauders]] from [[Lourna Dee's Tempest]]—including [[Quin Carree]] and [[Tempest Runner]] [[Lourna Dee]] herself—carried out a [[raid on Ferrix]].[[The High Republic: Tempest Breaker (script)|''The High Republic: Tempest Breaker'' script]] Ferrix was also the site of a [[Hostage negotiation on Ferrix|hostage negotiation]]''[[The High Republic Adventures Phase III - The Wedding Spectacular]]'' in [[228 BBY]]{{StarlightDate|''[[The High Republic Adventures Phase III - The Wedding Spectacular]]'', including the hostage negotiation on Ferrix,|one [[Standard year|year]] and a few [[Standard month|months]] after the destruction of Starlight Beacon|[[228 BBY]]}} that involved the [[Jedi Order]], with [[Jedi Master]] [[Kantam Sy]] overseeing the negotiation. The event happened to concur with the [[Mrala-Talisola Wedding|wedding]] of Sy's former [[Padawan]],[[The High Republic Adventures (2023) 6|''The High Republic Adventures'' (2023) 6]] the former [[Jedi]] [[Lula Mrala-Talisola|Lula Talisola]], on the Outer Rim world of [[Eriadu]] in the [[Occlusion Zone]]. Upset they would not be able to come if the negotiation dragged on, Sy worked hard to be able to attend the wedding and, right before it began, was able to arrive. During the [[Clone Wars]] that raged from [[22 BBY]] to [[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' Ferrix was a part of the [[Galactic Republic]]. In the direct aftermath of the war, however, the [[Galactic Empire]] [[Proclamation of the New Order|rose in its place]]. ===Aftermath of the Clone Wars=== {{Quote|Long live the Republic!''"
"''Free Ferrix!|Anti-Imperial protesters|}} [[File:FerrixCityCenter-TWBM.png|left|thumb|290x290px|The city center as seen from a shuttle ferry]] The Empire would later move to establish a presence on Ferrix, although local citizen [[Clem Andor]] believed that the Imperials would leave once they had shown their forces off. After [[Clone trooper|clone troopers]] were deployed to the [[planet]],{{Andor|Nobody's Listening!}} an anti-Imperial protest occurred, dubbed the "[[Rix Road Protest|Rix Road protest]]."{{SW|url=series/andor/andor-episode-7-announcement|text="Announcement" Episode Guide | Andor}} {{C|Trivia Gallery Image 5}} In town, a large contingent of [[Cloning|clone]] stormtroopers were pelted with [[stone]]s as they marched through the main square, prompting their [[Unidentified Imperial officer (Ferrix)|officer]] to order the [[trooper]]s to raise their weapons against the populace. [[Clem Andor|Andor]], who had been attempting to calm the crowd, was mistakenly accused of taking part in the protest and was subsequently [[Hanging|hanged]] in the town's square. In retaliation for his father's hanging, Andor's son [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian]] would later try to attack several clone troopers with a [[baton]], but was instead caught and arrested. ===Under Preox-Morlana=== {{main|Ambush on Ferrix}} {{Quote|P-P-Pre-Mor Authority is seeking a Kenari male resident of Ferrix for questioning. Citizens with any information should contact the Preox-Morlana Security HQ without d-d-delay.|[[B2EMO]] reads a bulletin released by Preox-Morlana Security|}} [[File:Premor logo.svg|right|thumb|290x290px|Despite Ferrix technically fell under the jurisdiction of the Preox-Morlana Corporation (logo pictured), the planet was mostly left to its own devices]] At some point, the Empire allowed the [[Consolidated Holdings of Preox-Morlana Corporation]] to run affairs on Ferrix, though it was not regularly patrolled, rather being left to its own devices. In [[5 BBY]], Clem Andor's son [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian]] traveled to the Preox-Morlana headquarters on Morlana-1 in an attempt to locate his missing [[Kenari (people)|Kenari]] sister, [[Kerri]]. During his travel he was confronted by two [[Tac-Corpo|corpos]] of the Preox-Morlana's corporate security branch, the [[Pre-Mor Authority Security Forces|Pre-Mor Enforcement]], and during the ensuing altercation he was forced to [[Death|kill]] them both. Pre-Mor [[Deputy Inspector]] [[Syril Karn]] identified and tracked the fleeing Cassian to his Ferrixian hometown and soon arrived to arrest him with a [[Pre-Mor Security Inspection team]] led by [[Sergeant]] [[Linus Mosk]]. Andor had however secured a meeting with [[Axis network|rebel]] [[spymaster]] [[Luthen Rael]] thanks to the intervention of [[Caleen Salyard|salvage yard]] owner [[Bix Caleen]] in order to sell him a [[Thief|stolen]] [[Imperial N-S9 Starpath Unit]], the sale taking place just as the Pre-Mor units' [[RK-392 mobile tac-pod|mobile Tac-Pods]] were landing on the city's scrapyards. A heavily armed Rael helped Andor escape the trap the corpos were setting up for him and thanks to a distraction afforded by a remotely-controlled [[Explosive charge|explosive]]-riddled [[speeder bike]] the duo were able to escape the city on board the spymaster's [[Luthen Rael's Fondor Haulcraft|Fondor Haulcraft]], leaving many injured or dead corpos behind them. ===Imperial occupation=== {{Quote|We've had each other, and Ferrix, our work, our days. We had each other, and they left us alone. We kept the trade lanes open, and they left us alone. We took their money and ignored them, we kept their engines churning, and the moment they pulled away, we forgot them. Because we had each other. We had Ferrix.|Maarva Andor|}} [[File:Blevin-on-Ferrix.jpg|left|thumb|290x290px|ISB lieutenant Blevin on Ferrix]] Following news of the incident, the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[officer]] responsible for the [[Morlani system]], [[Lieutenant]] [[Supervisor]] [[Blevin]] was dispatched to the Pre-Mor's [[Corporate Security Headquarters]] on Morlana One where he met with the trio of officers responsible for the disaster, leading to Ferrix{{Andor|Aldhani (episode)}} being placed under direct Imperial authority once more. A new Imperial [[Ferrix garrison|garrison]] was placed on Ferrix a day after the [[Ambush on Ferrix|incident]] with Preox-Morlana personnel removed from the system and re-assigned to other duties{{Andor|Daughter of Ferrix}} and the [[Hotel Rix|city hotel]] being taken over as the new Imperial headquarters on Ferrix. [[Captain]] [[Vanis Tigo]] was assigned by Blevin with overseeing the setup of the day-to-day Imperial Operations on Ferrix and was promoted to [[Prefect (Galactic Empire)|Prefect]] for the region after his request. With growing conflict between Blevin and fellow [[ISB Supervisor]] [[Dedra Meero]] during the regional supervisors' forums on [[Coruscant]], ISB [[Major]] [[Lio Partagaz|Partagaz]] gave control of the sector to Meero due to his agreeing with her suspicion of a growing, organized rebel network being responsible for the incident on Ferrix.{{Andor|The Axe Forgets}} The Imperial occupation caused much discomfort to the rebellious people of Ferrix. [[Stormtrooper]] units patrolled the once quiet streets and armed [[speeder]]s accompanied by [[Imperial security trooper]]s guarded all government buildings. Prominent resident and former [[president]] of the citizen society [[Daughters of Ferrix]] [[Maarva Carassi Andor|Maarva Andor]] vowed to overthrow Imperial rule, inspired by the [[Aldhani heist|attack]] on the [[Aldhani Garrison|Imperial]] [[Aldhani dam|headquarters]] on the planet [[Aldhani]], which unbeknownst to her was partly carried out by her son Cassian who was recruited by Luthen Rael on his network. Maarva made daily excursions on secret tunnels and passages next to the former hotel which housed the Prefecture headquarters but was severely injured and forced to stop. Her injury along with her age caused her to fall ill, but she refused to take the medicine [[doctor]] [[Mullmoy]] had prescribed her and eventually passed away. ===Revolution=== {{Quote|Ferrix has been hiding long enough.|Maarva Andor|}} [[File:Rix-Road-Rebellion.png|thumb|right|291px|Ferrix residents fought back against their Imperial occupiers]] During her [[Maarva's funeral procession|funeral procession]], a holographic message she had pre-recorded and broadcast by her [[droid]] [[B2EMO]] inspired the people of Ferrix to [[Ferrix Riot|rise up]] against the Empire and form a [[Ferrix resistance movement|resistance movement]],{{InsiderCite|221|Space Moms}} creating a riot spontaneously erupting as residents charged the Imperial barrier. An improvised explosive device thrown at the barrier by a resident turned the riot into a bloodbath as Imperials and Ferrixians were killed by the explosion, leading to Imperial troops being ordered to fire indiscriminately into the crowd. ==Society and culture== {{Quote|Stone and sky.|The people of Ferrix|}} [[File:Rip maarva andor.png|left|thumb|290x290px|A funerary stone was a symbolic artifact of a great deceased citizen of Ferrix]] Ferrix's exports were mainly scrap and salvaged tech. Many [[human]]s on Ferrix worked to salvage materials from decommissioned [[Starship|ships]] such as the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]]. Each worker was given a different set of gloves, with the gloves being hung on a wall before and after work. Ferrixians played songs at funerals and other public events using adhoc bands and amateurish musicians, "Unto Stone We Are" being one such piece. The daily routine on Ferrix was to go to work when the [[Time Grappler]] hit the [[beskar]] anvil using his hammers and to finish work when the Time Grappler hit the beskar anvil again. After this, the people of Ferrix would drink in cantinas or go back to their homes. The workers of Ferrix adhered to this structured schedule. Overall, workers trusted each other, were cooperative and respectful, and were generally friendly amongst each other. They stored their gear together in a public space, with each worker's gloves being hung on a large wall all together. Ferrix had a rudimentary warning system where residents would bang metal together to alert others of foreign intrusions or threats. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Ferrix should feel like a working town with a small community. And the whole logic of how we decided to build that as one big composite set on the back lot was based on that idea. You can get lost in it; when you're filming, you're not having to cut between sets.|Luke Hull|{{WebCite|url=https://www.theverge.com/23445550/star-wars-andor-production-costume-design-interview|text=Andor's designers approached it like a Star Wars period drama|author=Webster, Andrew|work=[[Wikipedia:The Verge|''The Verge'']]|archivedate=20221109181234}}}} Ferrix was first pictured in the sizzle reel for the ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' television series, which was released on [[December 10]], [[2020]].{{SWYouTube|gSW-pARyP-M|Sizzle Reel | Andor | Disney+|sw_url=video/sizzle-andor}} It was first identified in a [[LEGO]] set reveal during [[Celebration Anaheim (2022)|Celebration Anaheim]].{{SWYouTube|jqcv2RJ83nE|Star Wars Celebration LIVE! – DAY 2|nolive=1}} The planet first appeared in "[[Kassa (episode)|Kassa]]," the first episode of the series, which aired on [[September 21]], 2022.{{Twitter|starwars|status/1557442379975573504|[[Star Wars]]|date=2022-08-10|quote=This is what revolution looks like. Watch #Andor, a Star Wars Original Series, streaming only on @DisneyPlus September 21.|archivedate=20220810191942}} From the start, executive producer and writer [[Tony Gilroy]] found it was important for Ferrix to have an immersive culture{{SW|url=news/tony-gilroy-andor-interview|text="The Education of Cassian Andor": Creator Tony Gilroy Explores the Nuance of ''Andor''}} and a strong cultural heart.{{WebCite|url=https://uk.movies.yahoo.com/building-worlds-andor-ferrix-built-173536623.html|text=Building the Worlds of ‘Andor': How Ferrix Was Built Brick-by-Brick on a Backlot|author=Peterson, Karen M.|date=2022-10-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Yahoo! Movies|Yahoo! Movies]]|archivedate=20221020160200}} [[File:FerrixConceptArt.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Concept art of ''Venator''-class Star Destroyers being dismantled on Ferrix by Scott McInnes]] Gilroy, who stated the "mental build" of Ferrix took two years to develop,{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/08/andor-secrets-awards-insider|text=''Andor'': Inside the Making of a Perfect Star Wars Episode|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2023-08-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity_Fair_(magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20231024185917}} wanted the audience to understand that the Ferrixians came together and looked after each other. Production designer [[Luke Hull]] and Gilroy wanted to design an environment different from familiar ''Star Wars'' locations. They did not want to make the location a town in a [[desert]], and Hull was ardent on it not being a frontier town. To show the planet's culture, Gilroy and the crew spent a long time creating the planet's social structure, hierarchies, rules, and allegiances. Concept artist [[Scott McInnes]] created concept art of ''Venator''-class Star Destroyers being dismantled on Ferrix, and artist [[Vincent Jenkins]] created concept art of Cassian Andor preparing to shoot stormtroopers. Artist [[Chester Carr]]{{SW|url=andor-concept-art-gallery|text=Concept Art Gallery | Andor}} and Hull created a sketch of Rael and Cassian Andor escaping on a speeder bike. Hull also made sketches of the North Steps, the Ferrix hotel, the interior of the [[Andor household]], and Rael on Ferrix. To help ground the show's storytelling in a relatable human complexity and appeal to viewers, an entire{{Getty|url=thewaltdisneystudios/allaccess#!asset/gppr5wpqgb4t74974f8s|text=ANDOR Production Brief V3 FINAL 8-04-22|author=[[Gina McIntyre|McIntyre, Gina]]|date=2022-08-04}} Hull's team referenced [[Wikipedia:Amsterdam|Amsterdam]] in the [[1920s]], the period in which the city featured simple geometric and abstract shapes.{{Twitter|NatGeoTravel|status/1575274368460111874|[[Wikipedia:National Geographic Traveler|Nat Geo Travel]]|date=2022-09-28|quote=From post-war Scotland to 1920s Amsterdam, explore the locations that inspired the architecture of #Andor, an original series from Star Wars, now streaming only on @DisneyPlus.|archivedate=20220929235420}} Everything grew off of knowing Ferrix needing a big main street. After deciding Ferrix would be built, Hull's team had to find an overall look that stayed true to the franchise in a way that was not too dystopian. Due to the planet's economy of salvaging ship parts and metal, Hull envisioned the place with a sturdiness. Ferrix reminded him of longshoremen in [[Wikipedia:Belfast|Belfast]], [[Wikipedia:Northern Ireland|Northern Ireland]] building ships. Hull's team's origin for Ferrix was it began as a small outpost that gradually grew and expanded out of the hillside as the population grew. Hull made sure that the set felt like a working town with a small community. [[File:FerrixConstruction.png|thumb|right|200px|The Ferrix set being constructed in Little Marlow]] During planning, Hull's team accounted for the [[Wikipedia:Computer graphics|computer graphics]] and [[Wikipedia:Visual effects|VFX]] that would be added later, and it was built into the design. Hull's team team decided to build the town out of bricks, which had not been done in ''Star Wars'' before. Hull kept the color of the brick unchanged because he thought the clay and earthiness played into who the Ferrixians were. His team retrofitted the idea of dead Ferrixians' ashes getting baked into a brick and being put into the town. During the construction of Ferrix, the crew noticed that [[Wikipedia:Mars|Martian]]-like reds kept coming in, so [[Wikipedia:Lanzarote|Lanzarote]] in the [[Canary Islands]] became a good starting place to create the wider environment of Ferrix. Scenes on Ferrix were also filmed in Lanzarote's Green Lagoon; [[Wikipedia:Salinas de Janubio|Salinas de Janubio]], the Islands' largest [[Wikipedia:Salt evaporation pond|salt flat]];{{WebCite|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/travel/article/star-wars-film-movie-locations|text=8 places to visit if you love ‘Star Wars'|author=Williams, Starlight; McAndrews, Mary Beth|date=2017-12-11|work=[[Wikipedia:National Geographic|''National Geographic'']]|archivedate=20221128004036}} and other nearby locations. The backlot set was a functional shape full of usable buildings that were accessible through doors and windows. The sets included palatial homes, high-class brothels, and housing projects. Maarva Andor's house was crafted to explain her character. The interior and exterior of the house were the same set, making it fully three-dimensional.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-episode-8-toby-haynes-forest-whitaker-stellan-skarsgard-1235250954|text=‘Andor' Director Toby Haynes Talks That Forest Whitaker-Stellan Skarsgard Scene: “It Was a Career Highlight”|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-10-28|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20221029050743}} The set designers and costume shop collaborated to create the wall of gloves.{{SW|url=news/dressing-the-galaxy-designer-michael-wilkinson-defines-the-look-of-andor-s-costumes|text=Dressing the Galaxy: Designer Michael Wilkinson Defines the Look of Andor's Costumes}} Hull tried to make the [[Easter egg (virtual)|Easter eggs]] subtle and fit into the show. The Ferrix set managed to impress executive producer [[Kathleen Kennedy]] and director [[Toby Haynes]]. Costume designer [[Michael Wilkinson]] and his team spent a long time to establish carefully curated palettes of textures and colors for Ferrix to make the information clear for the viewers.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-interview-michael-wilkinson-star-wars|text='Andor's Costume Designer on Creating Cassian's Wardrobe and Returning for Season 2|author=Lovitt, Maggie|date=2022-11-14|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20221114190034}} They infused every costume with individualism to make it reflect the character it was worn by. During the beginning, Wilkinson told his team to consider many unique details to inform the design, including each character's job and source of clothing, and how their clothing reflects what they do, who they are, and what they value. Some of the costumes' silhouettes drew inspiration from [[Wikipedia:Japan|Japanese]] workwear, which were then abstracted and modernized. Wilkinson said that having costumes from an authentic and culturally resonant place would give the audience something they could connect with. [[File:BixCaleenConceptArt.jpg|thumb|left|120px|Concept art of Bix Caleen based on Michael Wilkinson's design]] The costume department also created logos and symbols for Ferrix's different brands, repair shops, and individual businesses, which deepened the planet's lore and tangibility. When the team created the Ferrixian clothing, they chose what they deemed the coolest and most interesting workwear elements between quilting, safety gear, and protective materials. Some of the stand-out characters, such as Bix Caleen, were given distinguishable silhouettes to help them stand out from a crowd. For the finale episode "[[Rix Road (episode)|Rix Road]]," the red was amped up to make it a very strong symbol of the spirit of Ferrix. Hull estimated that around 80-85% of the scenes on Ferrix were shot on the backlot set. According to Gilroy, everything on Ferrix was filmed first.{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-season-2-post-credits-scene-tony-gilroy-1235268962|text=‘Andor' Creator Tony Gilroy Talks Luthen's Good Day, That Post-Credit Scene and Season Two |author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20221123185515}} Haynes and the actors spent about a month shooting his six episodes' Ferrix scenes. After [[Wikipedia:Christmas|Christmas]], it was the coldest part of the shoot. When it snowed, the crew used heaters to burn the snow and keep the continuity. When [[Denise Gough]], the actor who plays [[Dedra Meero]], first shot on the Ferrix set, she was amazed by the high level of detail. Visual effects for Ferrix was split between [[Hybride]] and [[Industrial Light & Magic]]. Hybride worked on the town, based on the set, which was extended out to the larger city. [[Wikipedia:Chroma key|Green screens]] were used for certain Ferrix locations. ILM worked on what they called the north side big yard and the surrounding areas. They also built up the planet's architecture and made a design language for Ferrix. ILM was responsible for extending the Ferrix set to make it a busy hustling place with many workers and sparks everywhere. They made sure there was always something moving in the background to make it look like there was stuff going on all the time. For the ships on Ferrix, ILM started by referencing ships in the [[Lucasfilm Archives|archives]].{{WebCite|url=https://beforesandafters.com/2023/01/31/heres-how-industrial-light-magic-orchestrated-that-luthens-lightsaber-ship-in-andor|text=Here's how Industrial Light & Magic orchestrated Luthen's ‘lightsaber' ship in ‘Andor'|author=Failes, Ian|date=2023-01-31|work=[https://beforesandafters.com Befores and afters]|archivedate=20230201102819}} Composer [[Nicholas Britell]] inserted several metal sounds throughout Ferrix because of the masonry and metallurgy present in the planet's culture. Britell and Gilroy made some of those sounds together using the pipes in the latter's basement.{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/artisans/news/andor-composer-nicholas-britell-score-star-wars-1235383443|text=‘Andor' Composer Nicholas Britell Breaks Down His Score and Why He Incorporated Rustling Leaves|author=Burlingame, Jon|date=2022-09-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220926170019}} ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of
